title: Case studies
text: These studies look back at the largest up and down days since the SpaceX listing on June 12, 2026. Each one applies the journal’s method to a day whose outcome is already known: what moved, which channel drove it, what happened over the following five trading days, and what the episode teaches.

title: SpaceX adds 20% on its second day as an Iran deal lifts risk assets
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: SpaceX adds 20% on its second day as an Iran deal lifts risk assets
text:
Observation

SPCX rose 19.6% to $192.50, about 43% above its $135 offer price, on its second day of trading.
SPY gained 1.76% and QQQ 3.14%. The space group averaged +7.3% (RKLB +6.7%) and semiconductors +4.4%.
Crude oil fell 4.9% to $80.75 and XOM lost 4.1%. The VIX fell 8.4% to 16.2.
Defensive and healthcare groups were slightly negative.

title: SpaceX adds 20% on its second day as an Iran deal lifts risk assets
text:
Mechanism
Two separate things happened on the same day.
SpaceX: the flows channel.

Only about 5% of the company was sold in the offering, so the tradable supply was small.
Index providers had announced fast inclusion, so funds that track those indexes were expected to become forced buyers.
Heavy retail demand met that small supply, and the price rose without any new information about cash flows.

The broad market: the risk premium channel.

A reported US-Iran deal lowered the odds of an oil supply disruption.
Oil fell, which eased inflation pressure and lowered the premium investors demanded for risk.
Energy producers fell with oil while growth and semiconductor names led.

title: SpaceX adds 20% on its second day as an Iran deal lifts risk assets
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days SPCX fell 18.9%, QQQ fell 4.0% and SPY fell 2.6%. SpaceX gave back more than the whole second-day gain within a week.

title: SpaceX adds 20% on its second day as an Iran deal lifts risk assets
text:
Lesson
A price set by scarce supply and forced buyers is not a statement about value. When a move has no cash-flow news behind it, the question to ask is who had to buy and whether they are finished. Peers moved in sympathy on the way up and offered no protection on the way down.

title: Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting probe, and gold falls with it
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting probe, and gold falls with it
text:
Observation

NVDA fell 14.01% to $125.53. SMH fell 10.6%, QQQ 5.67% and SPY 3.64%.
The VIX rose 26.2% to 35.9.
Bonds rallied: TLT +1.37%, and the 10-year yield fell to 4.91%.
Gold did not: GLD fell 3.67%. Defensives (+1.1%) and healthcare (+0.9%) rose.

title: Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting probe, and gold falls with it
text:
Mechanism
Channel: the risk premium, amplified by flows.

Reuters reported that the SEC was examining Nvidia’s accounting.
An accounting question makes reported earnings less reliable, so investors demand a higher return to hold the stock.
The price fell without any change to revenue forecasts; the company had reported record results three days earlier.
Because Nvidia is one of the largest weights in the major indexes, its fall pulled the benchmarks down with it.
Gold falling on a day when bonds rose points to investors selling what they could to raise cash.

The gold side of this day is analysed in the journal entry of the same date.

title: Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting probe, and gold falls with it
text:
What happened next
Too recent to assess. The outcome is being tracked in the live journal.

title: Nvidia falls 14% on an accounting probe, and gold falls with it
text:
Lesson
Good earnings do not protect a stock when the question is whether the earnings can be trusted. Also, a safe asset does not always behave like one: in a forced selloff, the most liquid holdings are sold first, whatever their fundamentals.

title: Microsoft +15.5%, Meta -8%: the market prices the return on AI spending
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: Microsoft +15.5%, Meta -8%: the market prices the return on AI spending
text:
Observation

MSFT rose 15.51%, its largest one-day gain since 2008. META fell 7.95% on the same day.
AMD gained 13.0% and SMH 6.9%. SPY rose 1.68% and QQQ 3.30%.
Healthcare (-2.4%) and defensives (-1.6%) fell. The VIX dropped 17.3% to 17.1.
The 10-year yield ended at 4.66%, slightly higher on the day.

title: Microsoft +15.5%, Meta -8%: the market prices the return on AI spending
text:
Mechanism
Channel: cash flows.
Two companies in the same industry reported on the same evening and moved in opposite directions.

Microsoft showed cloud growth above expectations and did not raise its capital spending plans.
Meta missed on earnings, raised its spending forecast and reported a sharp fall in free cash flow.
The market rewarded evidence that AI spending was turning into revenue, and penalized spending without it.
Semiconductors rallied because Microsoft’s result supported continued demand for AI hardware.
Defensives were sold to fund the move back into growth.

Yields did not fall, so this was not a discount-rate rally. It was driven by earnings.

title: Microsoft +15.5%, Meta -8%: the market prices the return on AI spending
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days MSFT rose a further 10.8%, META recovered 9.4% and SPY rose 3.6%.

title: Microsoft +15.5%, Meta -8%: the market prices the return on AI spending
text:
Lesson
Markets price the surprise relative to expectations, not the level. When a theme is under doubt, the dispersion between companies inside it carries more information than the average. The question the market asked of AI spending that day was specific: where is the revenue?

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: stocks and bonds fall together
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: stocks and bonds fall together
text:
Observation

SPY fell 1.54% and QQQ 2.04%. NVDA fell 3.55%.
Crude oil rose 6.6% to $84.46. XOM gained 2.4% and the commodity group was the only one clearly positive.
Long Treasuries fell too: TLT lost 1.65%. The VIX rose 13.5% to 20.7.
The weakest groups were space (-6.4%), semiconductors (-4.2%) and cyclicals (-3.2%, with CAT -6.9%).

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: stocks and bonds fall together
text:
Mechanism
Channel: the risk-free rate, with a cash-flow effect on cyclicals.

An Iranian missile attack on US forces raised the risk of lost oil supply.
Oil jumped, which raised expected inflation on the day of a Federal Reserve decision.
Higher expected inflation raised the odds of rate increases, so bond prices fell and yields rose.
A higher discount rate hit the longest-duration equities hardest: space and semiconductors.
Higher fuel and input costs hit cyclicals through their margins.

The signature of an inflation shock is that stocks and bonds fall on the same day. In a growth scare, bonds would have rallied.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: stocks and bonds fall together
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days SPY rose 5.5%, NVDA 15.4% and MSFT 24.8%. Oil eased, and Microsoft’s results after that day’s close changed the subject.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: stocks and bonds fall together
text:
Lesson
An oil supply shock can be identified from three things moving together: energy up, bonds down, cyclicals down. It can also fade within days if no supply is actually lost. Before extrapolating a geopolitical move, check whether barrels have been removed from the market or only the fear of it.

text:
NoteRetrospective entry, written in hindsight

title: SpaceX day two: a float squeeze, and a forecast that failed
text:
Observation


SPCX +19.6% to $192.50 on its second day, about 43% above the $135 offer price.
QQQ +3.14%, SPY +1.76%. Space peers rose with it: RKLB +6.7%.
Oil -4.9% and XOM -4.1% on a reported US-Iran deal.

title: SpaceX day two: a float squeeze, and a forecast that failed
text:
Mechanism


Channel: flows.
Only about 5% of the company was sold, so few shares were available to trade.
Index funds were due to buy when the stock joined the indexes later in June.
Demand was large and supply small, so the price rose with no news about profits.

title: SpaceX day two: a float squeeze, and a forecast that failed
text:
Prediction


55% probability that SPCX closes higher on June 23 (five trading days) than $192.50.
Reasoning: the index funds had not bought yet, so more forced buying was still ahead.
Wrong if SPCX closes at or below $192.50 on June 23.

title: SpaceX day two: a float squeeze, and a forecast that failed
text:
Scoring


Wrong. SPCX fell 18.9% over the five days; QQQ fell 4.0%.
The broken link: I assumed the index buying was still to come. Traders who expected it had already bought in advance, so it was in the price.
Lesson: when a forced buyer is publicly known, ask who has already bought ahead of them.

title: Gold falls 9% in a week while yields decline: flows, not rates
text:
GLD closed at $322.87 on Nov 20, down from $369.36 on Nov 10 (-12.6%) and from $355.45 on Nov 13 (-9.2% on the week).
Spot gold ended the week near $3,535 an ounce, its lowest close in over a year.
Friday Nov 20 was the worst day: GLD -3.67% on about 23.6 million shares, roughly double its 10-day average.
Over the same week the 10-year Treasury yield fell from about 5.15% to 4.92%, and the 10-year real yield was nearly flat (2.91% to 2.88%).
Equities: the S&P 500 fell seven sessions in a row and the VIX closed near 36.
Silver fell more than 13% on the week.

title: Gold falls 9% in a week while yields decline: flows, not rates
text:
GLD closed at $322.87 on Nov 20, down from $369.36 on Nov 10 (-12.6%) and from $355.45 on Nov 13 (-9.2% on the week).
Spot gold ended the week near $3,535 an ounce, its lowest close in over a year.
Friday Nov 20 was the worst day: GLD -3.67% on about 23.6 million shares, roughly double its 10-day average.
Over the same week the 10-year Treasury yield fell from about 5.15% to 4.92%, and the 10-year real yield was nearly flat (2.91% to 2.88%).
Equities: the S&P 500 fell seven sessions in a row and the VIX closed near 36.
Silver fell more than 13% on the week.

title: Gold falls 9% in a week while yields decline: flows, not rates
text:
Mechanism

My first explanation: the risk-free rate channel.

Gold pays no interest.
When real yields are high, holding gold means giving up more income.
Investors shift from gold to bonds, and gold falls.

Test against the data: yields fell last week, so this channel predicts gold flat or higher. Gold fell 9%. The rate story explains the decline since January, but not this week.
Revised explanation: the flows channel.

Equities fell sharply and volatility spiked.
Leveraged investors faced margin calls and needed cash.
They sold liquid assets, including gold, regardless of its fundamentals.
Evidence: double the normal volume, gold’s worst day matching the equity market’s worst day, and silver falling harder than gold.

title: Gold falls 9% in a week while yields decline: flows, not rates
text:
Prediction


55% probability that GLD closes above $322.87 on Nov 30 (five trading days).
Reasoning: forced selling ends when the selling pressure in equities eases, even if yields do not move.
Wrong if GLD closes at or below $322.87 on Nov 30.
What I will watch: if the VIX falls and gold still declines, the flows explanation is wrong and rates or the dollar matter more than I think.
Disclosure: I hold a small position in GLD.

title: Gold falls 9% in a week while yields decline: flows, not rates
text:
Scoring

To be scored after the close on Nov 30.

title: Microsoft up 15%, Meta down 8%: a bet on post-earnings drift
text:
NoteRetrospective entry, written in hindsight



Written in November 2026, after the outcome was known, to practise the journal’s method on a past market day. The prediction is the one the mechanism would have implied that evening. This entry is excluded from the scored record, which begins with the entry of November 20, 2026.

title: Microsoft up 15%, Meta down 8%: a bet on post-earnings drift
text:
Observation


MSFT +15.51%, its best day since 2008. META -7.95% on the same day.
AMD +13.0%, SMH +6.9%, QQQ +3.30%.
Healthcare -2.4% and defensives -1.6%. The 10-year yield rose slightly to 4.66%.

title: Microsoft up 15%, Meta down 8%: a bet on post-earnings drift
text:
Mechanism


Channel: cash flows.
Microsoft beat expectations on cloud growth and did not raise its spending plans.
Meta missed on earnings and raised its spending forecast, and its free cash flow fell sharply.
The market rewarded AI spending that was already producing revenue.
Yields did not fall, so this rally came from earnings, not from lower rates.

title: Microsoft up 15%, Meta down 8%: a bet on post-earnings drift
text:
Prediction


60% probability that MSFT outperforms META over the next five trading days (to August 6).
Reasoning: after a large earnings surprise, prices often keep drifting in the same direction as analysts revise estimates.
Wrong if META returns more than MSFT over that window.

title: Microsoft up 15%, Meta down 8%: a bet on post-earnings drift
text:
Scoring

Right, narrowly. MSFT +10.8%, META +9.4%.
The link held, but Meta rebounded almost as much once the whole market rallied.
Lesson: a relative call (A beats B) removed the market direction from the bet, which is why it survived a strong week for everything.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: a sound mechanism, a wrong call
text:
Observation


SPY -1.54%, QQQ -2.04%, NVDA -3.55%.
Oil +6.6% to $84.46 after an Iranian missile attack on US forces. XOM +2.4%.
Bonds fell too: TLT -1.65%. VIX +13.5% to 20.7.
Worst groups: space -6.4%, semiconductors -4.2%, cyclicals -3.2%.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: a sound mechanism, a wrong call
text:
Mechanism


Channel: the risk-free rate.
Higher oil raises expected inflation.
Higher expected inflation raises the chance of Fed rate increases, so yields rise and bond prices fall.
A higher discount rate hurts long-duration stocks the most.
Cyclicals were hit separately through higher fuel and input costs.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: a sound mechanism, a wrong call
text:
Prediction


55% probability that SPY closes lower on August 5 (five trading days) than $727.65.
Reasoning: an oil shock that lifts yields keeps pressure on stocks until oil comes back down.
Wrong if SPY closes above $727.65 on August 5.

title: An oil shock on a Fed day: a sound mechanism, a wrong call
text:
Scoring


Wrong. SPY rose 5.5% over the five days.
The broken link: oil did not stay high. It fell 10.9% over the same five days as tensions cooled.
A second force arrived that I had not weighed: Microsoft reported that evening and rose 15.5% the next day.
Lesson: the mechanism was sound, but it depended on oil staying up. State the condition in the prediction, and check the earnings calendar before predicting an index.

title: The post-election AI selloff: pricing a risk, not a law
text:
NoteRetrospective entry, written in hindsight



Written in November 2026, after the outcome was known, to practise the journal’s method on a past market day. The prediction is the one the mechanism would have implied that evening. This entry is excluded from the scored record, which begins with the entry of November 20, 2026.

title: The post-election AI selloff: pricing a risk, not a law
text:
Observation


SPY -4.41%, QQQ -6.49%: the worst day since April 2025.
NVDA -9.26%, AMD -17.26%, SMH -11.2%. VIX +69.7% to 28.2.
Safe assets rose: TLT +0.21%, GLD +0.81%. The 10-year yield fell to 4.84%.

title: The post-election AI selloff: pricing a risk, not a law
text:
Mechanism


Channel: cash flows and the risk premium.
A Democratic sweep in the midterms raised fear of new rules on data-center building.
Slower building would mean less revenue for chipmakers, so they were repriced.
Yields fell, so the discount rate was not the cause.

title: The post-election AI selloff: pricing a risk, not a law
text:
Prediction


55% probability that QQQ closes higher on November 12 (five trading days) than $647.05.
Reasoning: a policy scare is usually priced at its worst case on day one, before anyone knows what will actually pass.
Wrong if QQQ closes at or below $647.05 on November 12.

title: The post-election AI selloff: pricing a risk, not a law
text:
Scoring

Right. QQQ +6.4%, SPY +3.3%.
The link held: brokerages argued that extreme regulation was unlikely and buyers returned.
Lesson: a probability near 50% was honest here. The outcome was good, but the evidence that evening was thin.

Observation


QQQ -3.47%, SPY -1.77%.
AMD -10.88%, SMH -6.98%, NVDA -4.22%. Intel fell 28.6% on its results.
Defensives +1.3%, TLT +0.43%. GLD -3.47%.

title: Intel and the AI-spending selloff: why it continued
text:
Mechanism


Channel: cash flows.
Intel and Amazon results raised doubt that AI spending would earn an adequate return.
The doubt applied to the whole hardware chain, so semiconductors fell together.
Money moved into defensives and bonds: a rotation out of one theme, not a rush for cash.

title: Intel and the AI-spending selloff: why it continued
text:
Prediction


60% probability that SMH underperforms SPY over the next five trading days (to November 6).
Reasoning: a doubt about cash flows lasts until new information answers it, and none was scheduled.
Wrong if SMH returns more than SPY over that window.

title: Intel and the AI-spending selloff: why it continued
text:
Scoring

Right. SMH -11.2%, SPY -2.7%.
The link held: no new information arrived to settle the doubt, and the election added a second worry.
Lesson: ask what would end the selloff. If nothing on the calendar can answer the question, expect it to continue.

text:
Observation


SPY +2.37%, QQQ +3.54%, AMD +13.26%.
NVDA -4.27% to $178.67, the one large chip stock that fell.
Oil -4.4%, VIX -22.3% to 19.9.

title: The rebound Nvidia missed
text:
Mechanism


Market: lower oil eased inflation worry, and buyers returned after the previous week.
Nvidia: company-specific risk premium. The company said it was examining claims of a foreign intelligence effort tied to its chief executive.
Investors demanded more return to hold that one stock, so it fell while its peers rose.

title: The rebound Nvidia missed
text:
Prediction


60% probability that NVDA underperforms SMH over the next five trading days (to November 16).
Reasoning: governance problems are rarely settled in one announcement, so more bad news was more likely than a quick all-clear.
Wrong if NVDA returns more than SMH over that window.

title: The rebound Nvidia missed
text:
Scoring

Right. NVDA -12.6%, SMH -5.2%. The chief executive resigned on November 12.
The link held: the story developed over several disclosures.
Lesson: when a leader diverges from its sector on company news, treat the first move as the start of the repricing, not the end.

title: SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
Observation


SPY +1.80% to a record, QQQ +3.40%.
Oil -5.7% to $75.77 on hopes of a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. TLT +0.77%.
SPCX +9.43% to $125.33 before its first earnings report, due after the close.

title: SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
Mechanism


Market: the risk-free rate channel. Lower oil, lower inflation pressure, lower yields, so stocks and bonds rose together.
SpaceX: positioning. Buyers bid the stock up 9% before knowing the numbers.
That raised the bar: the report now had to beat the higher expectation built into the price.

title: SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
Prediction


55% probability that SPCX closes lower on August 5 than $125.33.
Reasoning: a large run-up into an event leaves little room for a good result, and capital spending had just punished Meta.
Wrong if SPCX closes above $125.33 on August 5.

title: SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
Scoring

Right. SPCX fell 13.6% the next day: revenue beat expectations but capital spending rose sharply.
Over five trading days, though, SPCX was up 6.4%.
Lesson: the horizon is part of the prediction. The same view was right at one day and wrong at five.

1d % and 5d % are close-to-close returns over one and five trading days.
vs 20d / 50d / 200d avg % show how far the latest close sits above (positive) or below (negative) its 20-, 50- and 200-day moving average: the short-, medium- and long-term trend.
trend is a rule-based label: Up when the close is above the 50-day average and the 50-day is above the 200-day; Down when both are reversed; Mixed otherwise. It describes the current trend. It is not a forecast and not a recommendation to buy or sell.
Prices are daily closes from Yahoo Finance, adjusted for splits and dividends.

title: The worst day since April 2025: a policy shock to the AI build-out
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: The worst day since April 2025: a policy shock to the AI build-out
text:
Observation

SPY fell 4.41%, QQQ 6.49% and IWM 4.59%.
NVDA fell 9.26%, AMD 17.26% and SMH 11.2%. The space group averaged -12.4%.
The VIX rose 69.7% to 28.2.
Safe assets behaved normally: TLT +0.21%, GLD +0.81%, and the 10-year yield fell to 4.84%.

title: The worst day since April 2025: a policy shock to the AI build-out
text:
Mechanism
Channel: cash flows and the risk premium, amplified by flows.

The midterm elections produced a sweep for the Democrats.
Investors feared new regulation of data-center development, which would slow the AI build-out.
A slower build-out means lower expected revenue for chipmakers and their suppliers, so those stocks were repriced.
A volatility jump of that size typically forces strategies that target a fixed level of risk to cut positions, which would have added to the selling. I have not verified positioning data for this day.

Yields fell on the day and growth stocks still collapsed. That rules out the discount rate as the cause: this was about expected cash flows and uncertainty.

title: The worst day since April 2025: a policy shock to the AI build-out
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days SPY recovered 3.3% and QQQ 6.4%, after several brokerages argued that extreme regulation was unlikely. NVDA fell a further 8.5% for reasons specific to the company.

title: The worst day since April 2025: a policy shock to the AI build-out
text:
Lesson
The market priced a risk, not a law. Policy shocks tend to be priced at their worst case on the first day and revised as the realistic range becomes clearer. It is also worth comparing gold here with November 20: on this day gold rose, a normal flight to safety; two weeks later it fell with stocks, which pointed to forced selling.

title: Intel’s worst day since 1974 turns AI-spending doubts into a sector selloff
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: Intel’s worst day since 1974 turns AI-spending doubts into a sector selloff
text:
Observation

QQQ fell 3.47% and SPY 1.77%.
AMD fell 10.88%, SMH 6.98% and NVDA 4.22%. The space group averaged -6.8%.
Defensives (+1.3%) and healthcare (+0.5%) rose. TLT gained 0.43% and the 10-year yield ended at 4.93%.
GLD fell 3.47%. The VIX rose 12.9% to 19.4.

title: Intel’s worst day since 1974 turns AI-spending doubts into a sector selloff
text:
Mechanism
Channel: cash flows.

Intel fell 28.6% after its results, and Amazon’s report added to concern about the cost of AI infrastructure.
Investors questioned whether the industry’s capital spending would earn an adequate return.
That doubt was applied to the whole hardware supply chain, so semiconductors were repriced together.
Money rotated into defensives and bonds, which is an orderly move away from one theme, not a rush for cash.

The dispersion inside the sector is informative: NVDA fell less than half as much as AMD, so investors were still ranking companies and not selling the group indiscriminately.
Open question. Gold fell 3.5% on a day when bonds rose. A safe asset falling alongside equities can indicate selling to cover losses elsewhere. I would need positioning data to confirm it.

title: Intel’s worst day since 1974 turns AI-spending doubts into a sector selloff
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days QQQ fell a further 5.0%, NVDA 8.8% and AMD 11.0%. The selling continued.

title: Intel’s worst day since 1974 turns AI-spending doubts into a sector selloff
text:
Lesson
Compare this with July 29. A geopolitical shock reversed within days because the feared event did not happen. A repricing based on doubts about cash flows persisted, because nothing arrived to answer the doubt. The cause of a selloff says a lot about how long it lasts.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%
text:
Observation

SPY rose 2.37%, QQQ 3.54% and IWM 3.23%.
AMD gained 13.26% and the space group averaged +11.5%.
NVDA fell 4.27% to $178.67, the only large semiconductor name to decline.
Crude oil fell 4.4% to $86.85 and the VIX dropped 22.3% to 19.9.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%
text:
Mechanism
The market: the risk-free rate and a falling risk premium.

Oil fell, which eased inflation concern.
Analysts argued the previous week’s selloff had overstated the regulatory risk.
Buyers returned to the names that had fallen most.

Nvidia: company-specific risk premium.

The company said it was examining claims of a foreign intelligence effort connected to its chief executive.
That raised governance and key-person risk for one company only.
Investors demanded a higher return to hold it, so it fell while its peers rallied.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%
text:
What happened next
Over the following five trading days NVDA fell a further 12.6% as the chief executive resigned, while SPY lost 1.7%.

title: A rebound without its leader: the market gains 2.4% while Nvidia falls 4.3%
text:
Lesson
When the leading stock of a sector diverges from the sector on company news, the divergence is the information. Governance events are rarely resolved in one disclosure, so the first day’s move is usually not the full repricing.

title: Record highs as oil falls; SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
NoteRetrospective case study



Written in November 2026, after the event, as a training exercise. It contains no prediction and is not part of the scored record. Price figures come from the project data file; news facts are sourced at the end.

title: Record highs as oil falls; SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
Observation

SPY rose 1.80% to a record close and QQQ rose 3.40%.
Crude oil fell 5.7% to $75.77. TLT gained 0.77% and the 10-year yield ended at 4.63%.
SPCX rose 9.43% to $125.33 ahead of its first report as a public company, still below its $135 offer price.
Space (+8.1%), semiconductors (+4.9%) and cyclicals (+2.8%) led. Healthcare was the only negative group.

title: Record highs as oil falls; SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
Mechanism
Channel: the risk-free rate, plus cash flows from earnings.
This was the mirror image of July 29.

Hopes for a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz pushed oil lower.
Lower oil eased inflation pressure, so bond yields fell.
A lower discount rate lifted long-duration equities, and stocks and bonds rose together.
Strong results and guidance from industrial and software companies added a cash-flow reason to buy.

SpaceX: positioning ahead of an event. The stock rose 9% before the numbers were known, which raised the bar the report had to clear.

title: Record highs as oil falls; SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
What happened next
SpaceX reported revenue above expectations after the close, but capital spending rose sharply and the stock fell 13.6% the next day. SPY was flat over the following five trading days.

title: Record highs as oil falls; SpaceX runs up into its first earnings report
text:
Lesson
A run-up into an event is a bet on the outcome, and it leaves less room for a good result to be rewarded. The reaction also repeated the July 30 pattern: revenue alone was not enough when spending surprised on the high side.

title: About
text: Market Journal is a daily research journal written by Blaire (Meina) Bian.

title: About
text:
What it is
Each entry takes one market move and works through it in four steps:

Observation: what moved, by how much, relative to the benchmark.
Mechanism: which channel drove it (cash flows, the risk-free rate, the risk premium, or flows) and the causal chain behind it.
Prediction: a testable call with a deadline and a probability.
Scoring: whether the call was right, and which link in the reasoning held or broke.

Every entry is committed to version control, so each prediction carries a timestamp that precedes its outcome. Entries dated before November 20, 2026 are retrospective exercises, labelled as written in hindsight and excluded from the scored record.

title: About
text:
Why
To build calibrated, mechanism-level judgment about how macroeconomic, policy, and company-level shocks transmit into asset prices. The journal is paired with a simulated portfolio so that each view is tested with a position.

title: About
text:
More detail
The full framework, including the factor map and the rules for the simulated portfolio, is in the project README.
This is a personal learning project. Nothing here is investment advice.
